title: React
blurb: React core, hooks, performance patterns, state, data fetching and tooling.

quiz.question: Why should list items have a stable key (not the array index) when the list can reorder?
options: Keys make rendering faster in every case
React uses keys to match elements between renders; index keys attach state to the wrong items after reorders or inserts
quiz.explanation: Keys give list items a stable identity. With index keys, inserting or reordering shifts identities, so component state and DOM (e.g., input values) end up on the wrong item.

quiz.question: What does the dependency array of useEffect control?
options: When the effect re-runs: after renders where any listed value changed
quiz.explanation: With [] the effect runs after mount only; with values it re-runs when any of them changes (compared with Object.is); with no array it runs after every render. The cleanup runs before the next run and on unmount.

quiz.question: Calling setCount(count + 1) three times in one click handler increments count by…
quiz.explanation: All three calls read the same count from the current render, and updates are batched. Use the updater form setCount(c => c + 1) to increment by 3.

quiz.question: What does the React Compiler (React 19 era) mainly do?
options: Automatically memoizes components and values, reducing the need for manual useMemo/useCallback
quiz.explanation: The compiler analyses components at build time and inserts memoization, so most manual useMemo, useCallback and React.memo becomes unnecessary — as long as components follow the Rules of React.

quiz.question: In the Next.js App Router, React Server Components…
options: Render on the server, can fetch data directly, and ship no component JavaScript to the client
quiz.explanation: Server Components render on the server and send their output; interactivity (state, effects, event handlers) needs a Client Component marked with 'use client'.

problems.title: Stale closure bug
problems.prompt: useEffect(() => { const id = setInterval(() => setCount(count + 1), 1000); return () => clearInterval(id); }, []); The counter stops at 1. Why, and how do you fix it?
hints: What value of count does the interval capture?
problems.solution: The effect runs once and the interval callback closes over count from the first render (0), so it keeps setting 1. Use the functional update setCount(c => c + 1) (keeping [] deps), or include count in the dependency array so the interval is recreated.

problems.title: Fetching data in an effect correctly
problems.prompt: A component fetches /api/user/:id in useEffect. When id changes quickly, an older response sometimes overwrites the newer one. Fix it.
problems.solution: Create an AbortController in the effect, pass its signal to fetch, and abort in the cleanup; ignore AbortError. Alternatively set an ignore flag in cleanup and skip setState when it's set. In real apps use a data library (TanStack Query) or framework loaders, which handle races and caching.
